research_question: Which observationally permitted late-time expansion histories lead to distinct cosmic-fate classes, and which measurements can discriminate them without extrapolating finite-redshift fits beyond their stated domain?

subhypotheses.claim: Finite-redshift constraints do not by themselves determine the a-to-infinity continuation of dark energy.
Expansion fate and false-vacuum decay are separable mechanisms requiring separate evidence.
Finite-time disruption is conditional on sustained phantom-like dynamics and cannot be inferred from acceleration alone.
A fate-oriented, multi-probe design should report the discriminating observable and the remaining observational non-identifiability.

writing_rules: Do not state a minimum time to universal death as an established observation.
Do not turn a fitted w0-wa parametrization into an asymptotic future law unless an explicit continuation assumption is declared.
Do not call a planned analysis an observed result.
Report vacuum decay separately from expansion fate.
Classify evidence as direct, conditional, background, or unresolved.
